family_questions.question: Does any Congress set read clearly as Congress, and if none does, what would?
family_questions.answer: No. Without its label, no set names Congress at 48 px. Set A reads as a city hall, set B as an arena or a signal, and set C as two signals. Set B comes nearest, because it is the only one that reads as a legislative chamber, and with the label beside it a reader takes it for the House at once. What would read: the body in session. Draw the members, the rostrum they face and the benches they sit on. Members on the front bench as Civic Line heads and shoulders seen from behind turn the room into a body. Solid curved benches stop the rows reading as a signal. A rostrum about a third of the drawing's width, stepped in three tiers with the red on the top tier, gives the eye the House's own landmark. I tested this direction with three rough sketches in my scratch folder: the stepped rostrum alone read as a podium or a cake, and the version with members read as an assembly facing a podium, the closest to a legislature. None named Congress without the label. Most readers know Congress by the Capitol dome, which Rule 01.6 keeps out, so the label will name it and the drawing's job is to make the label land at once. Rescore after the fix round: the reworked set B reads as the House in session, members facing a stepped rostrum, and the label Congress lands on it at once. No set names Congress without its label, and the board says so (D2-620).

family_questions.question: Keep every action bare and draw only Error, Success and Warning in a shape?
family_questions.answer: Yes. Ringed actions measure as near twins of each other (Close B and Pause B 0.973, Play B and Pause B 0.958), above the closest pair of Civic Line masters (0.964), so a toolbar of rings loses the shapes a reader tells apart. Each control already has its own 44 px target and outline, so a ring repeats it. The status marks need a shape, because a bare check means selected and a bare exclamation mark is punctuation. For the ring and frame options this means they stop being per-icon choices: picking Close B and Arrow A together would break the family. Show the enclosure once, on one family card that sets the recommended picks bare with shaped status marks beside the same set all ringed, so Dustin decides the treatment once. Each action card then offers bare pictures only, and the three status marks keep shapes that differ from each other: Error a closed circle, Success an open circle, Warning a triangle. Rescore after the fix round: done (D2-621). The family card leads the plate and shows both rows at 24 and 16 px on both grounds, with the atlas stepper in use; the bare set has no flagged pair, and the ringed set has 29.

family_questions.question: Pediments (Civic Line designer's question 7)
family_questions.answer: Agree with the designer: treat a pediment as part of the classical front and keep it out. That points to B for CL-059 and C for R-48. The A options keep theirs as the DR-135 record. Recorded as D2-623.
